headline: Pulse Asia: 51% Say Sara Duterte Should Testify in Impeachment Trial
seoTitle: Pulse Asia: 51% Say Sara Duterte Should Testify in Impeachment Trial
seoDescription: The September survey measured public opinion before later October developments; 34% opposed a personal appearance.
deck: The September survey measured public opinion before later October developments; 34% opposed a personal appearance.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What the survey found
paragraphs: Fifty-one percent of Filipino adults said Vice President Sara Duterte should personally testify in the Senate impeachment trial, according to Pulse Asia’s September survey, released on October 14.

The pollster’s published tables show 34% taking the opposite position, 14% undecided and 1% declining to answer. These figures describe respondents’ preferences, not a ruling on the case or an assessment of guilt.

sections.heading: How it was measured
paragraphs: Pulse Asia interviewed 2,400 adults aged 18 and older face to face from September 17 to 24. The national margin of error is plus or minus two percentage points at a 95% confidence level.
The fieldwork predates October developments in the proceedings. The results therefore cannot establish how respondents reacted to events after September 24.

sections.heading: How to read the result
paragraphs: Readers should distinguish support for personal testimony from support for a particular verdict. The question asks whether the vice president should appear and testify; it does not decide the allegations.
Consult the original questionnaire and tables when comparing survey headlines. Survey dates, question wording and the population being measured are essential context.
